definitions.explanation: a type of oily fish commonly eaten in Japan

examples.japanese: {鯖|さば}の{塩焼|しおや}きが{好|す}きだ。
{鯖|さば}の{味噌煮|みそに}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made mackerel simmered in miso.

examples.japanese: {新鮮|しんせん}な{鯖|さば}は{刺身|さしみ}でも{食|た}べられる。
examples.english: Fresh mackerel can be eaten as sashimi.

notes:
COMMON JAPANESE FISH:
{鯖|さば} is one of the most commonly eaten fish in Japan.

COMMON PREPARATIONS:
- {鯖|さば}の{塩焼|しおや}き - salt-grilled mackerel
- {鯖|さば}の{味噌煮|みそに} - mackerel simmered in miso
- {鯖寿司|さばずし} - mackerel sushi
- {しめ鯖|しめさば} - vinegared/cured mackerel
- {鯖缶|さばかん} - canned mackerel

TYPES:
- {真鯖|まさば} - Pacific mackerel
- ごま{鯖|さば} - spotted mackerel

IDIOM:
{鯖|さば}を{読|よ}む - to fudge numbers, to miscount (literally "to misread mackerel")

HEALTH NOTE:
{鯖|さば} is rich in DHA and EPA, omega-3 fatty acids good for health.

FAMOUS PRODUCTION AREAS:
- {福井|ふくい}{県|けん} - Fukui Prefecture (famous for {鯖|さば}{街道|かいどう})
